- When sentiment is negative (especially -1.00) in the last few days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a recent spike in price (e.g., >75), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days; cap forecast decline to 5–10% below peak or align with 3–5 day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., 1.00) and price is falling, model often underreacts; increase forecast slope slightly or add 1–2% upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward bias by 1–3% for first 7–10 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply mean reversion to 14-day rolling average for next 7–14 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after model forecast peak, model often fails to recognize momentum reversal — add 1–2 day lag correction: forecast next day = previous day’s true value + 0.5x (true - forecast) if true drops >5%.
